narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a setup utility. You move through Mark's work the way you'd configure a machine. A title bar names the system, tabs split it into Work, About and Contact, an item list carries the projects with dates and bracketed status, and an "Item Specific Help" pane explains whatever the selection bar is on. The key legend pinned to the bottom is the real set of actions. Every key in it works, and so does every pointer click. It's a configuration screen, not the dark "terminal portfolio" of prompts, typing effects and card grids.

Everything sits on a character-cell grid in one monospace face. Horizontal measure is counted in ch, structure is drawn with box rules, and emphasis comes from inverse video, not from shadows, gradients or rounded surfaces. It's dense on purpose: ruled panes hold key/value rows, layer flags and tabular timestamps, the way a BIOS screen packs a lot into one view without feeling crowded.

Five themes reskin the same screen. The defaults are Catppuccin Latte (light) and Mocha (dark), and Frappé, Macchiato and a Borland CGA theme can be picked from the menu. Every theme fills the same role tokens, so a component never knows which theme it's in.
keyCharacteristics: One monospace face (SauceCodePro NFM 400/700; BigBlueTerm437 NFM in Borland), ligatures off, on a character-cell grid.
Inverse-video title bar and key legend. Key caps invert a second time.
Box-drawing panes: 1px single rule at rest, 3px double rule for focus, title inset in the top rule.
An inverse selection bar that drives the help pane, from the keyboard or the pointer.
Bracketed status [Live] [Soon] [Private], [x] layer flags and [ Label ] buttons.
Square corners everywhere. Flat, with one exception: the theme menu's Turbo Vision window shadow.
Five role-token themes: Latte, Frappé, Macchiato, Mocha, Borland.

rules.name: The Inverse Video Rule
rules.body: The title bar and key legend are true inverse video. The bar field is the theme's text colour and its text is the base colour. Key caps invert again: a base-colour cap with the letter in the selection hue (mauve in Catppuccin; white on CGA blue in Borland). Never tint the bars with a brand colour or a translucent fill.

rules.name: The One Selection Rule
rules.body: The selection colour marks the one thing that's chosen or about to act: the selected list row, the active tab, the primary button, a hovered or focused button, a highlighted menu row and selected text. It always comes paired with its own selection-text colour. Never use it for decoration.

rules.name: The Bracket Status Rule
rules.body: The ok, warn and priv colours colour only the brackets of [Live], [Soon] and [Private]. The word stays in the text colour. On the selection bar the brackets take the selection-text colour. These three are signal colours, not text colours.

rules.name: The Role Token Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a role token (base, panel, text, muted, rule, bar, key, selection, accent, ok, warn, priv) defined in all five themes. Components use roles only. The one place a literal hex is allowed in markup is the theme menu's swatches, which preview the themes themselves.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: One monospace family per theme: SauceCodePro NFM at 400 and 700 with ligatures off, or BigBlueTerm437 NFM in Borland. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and colour alone. Never add a second family, an italic or a system display face.

rules.name: The Cell Grid Rule
rules.body: Horizontal measure is counted in characters: 1ch and 2ch padding, 13ch and 16ch label columns, a 2ch cursor column and a 9ch status column. Line lengths are capped in ch (40 to 68ch). Vertical rhythm is set in rem.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No kicker or eyebrow text above headings, and pane titles never repeat the page heading. The project header pane is titled "Overview", not the project name. The inset pane title is the only label a block gets.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: Every first viewport fits on one screen. At 1024px and up, the Main and Help panes stretch down to the legend (min-height calc(100svh - 11.5rem)), and the help pane's preview screen is capped at min(30vh, 320px) and cropped from the top.

rules.name: The Window Shadow Rule
rules.body: The theme menu casts a hard, unblurred shadow one character cell right and 0.6rem down (1ch 0.6rem 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35)). This is the Turbo Vision window shadow, part of this world and not a costume. It's the only hard shadow allowed and the only drop shadow of any kind. Every other surface is flat.

rules.name: The Square Cell Rule
rules.body: Every corner is square (0 radius): panes, buttons, key caps, inputs, menus and screenshots. A radius anywhere breaks the character grid.

rules.name: The Double Frame Rule
rules.body: A pane at rest has a 1px single rule. A pane that holds focus gets a 3px double rule, and while focus is inside it (:focus-within) the double rule switches to the accent colour. Every rule colour holds at least 3:1 against the field it sits on.

rules.name: The Instant Swap Rule
rules.body: Motion is instant state swaps, like a real TUI. Selection, hover inversion, menu open and theme change all happen in a single frame. No transitions, easing, fades or typing effects.

rules.name: The Labelled Plate Rule
rules.body: Every screen image says what it is in the right of its caption: [Screenshot] for a capture of the real product, [Illustration] for a labelled drawing of a private tool. Every shipping raster has a .webp.json provenance sidecar.

dos: **Do** build every surface out of the same parts: title bar, tabs, box-drawn panes with inset titles, an item list with a selection bar, and the pinned key legend.
**Do** set all text in the one monospace face with `font-variant-ligatures: none`, at 1rem / 1.55 for body and 700 for names, titles and key caps.

**Do** make every shortcut real and show it in the legend: W/A/C for the tabs (underlined letter), E email, R résumé, I LinkedIn, T theme, ↑↓ or j k select (in the project list and the theme menu, which previews themes live), Enter open, Esc back, ← → previous/next project.
**Do** keep the selected item and the "Item Specific Help" pane in sync for both pointer and keyboard selection.
**Do** define every new colour role in all five themes and check it in each. Text holds 4.5:1 and rules hold 3:1 against their field.
**Do** persist the theme choice in localStorage ("theme") and fall back to Latte or Mocha through prefers-color-scheme when it's Auto.
**Do** use native box-drawing and TUI glyphs (└ ▸ ↵ ● [x] [ ]) as structure. They're the world's own characters.
**Do** label screen images [Screenshot] or [Illustration], and ship each raster with its provenance sidecar.
donts: **Don't** add a kicker or eyebrow line above a heading, or title a pane with the page heading.
**Don't** round a corner, blur a shadow, or add any shadow other than the theme menu's window shadow.
**Don't** animate. No transitions, fades, typing effects or blinking cursors.
**Don't** set running text in the ok, warn or priv colours. They're bracket and stroke colours, and in Latte they fall under 3:1 on the base field.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or a proportional fallback for headings.
**Don't** turn it into a terminal: no shell prompts, no fake command lines, no project cards in a grid.
**Don't** pair the selection colour with anything but its own selection-text colour.
